t: In front of you in Parliament Square is a bronze statue of Lord Palmerston, standing on a granite pedestal. Thomas Woolner sculpted it, and it was unveiled in 1876. Woolner was a founding member of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, and its only sculptor. Edward Middleton Barry designed the setting, and Henry Young cast the bronze. Palmerston was prime minister from 1855 to 1858, and again from 1859 until his death in 1865. He was the first Liberal prime minister, and he dominated British foreign policy at the height of imperial power. The statue is Grade II listed.
